title: Attested Key Rotation Runbook — Terraform interop for air-gapped VPCs (v0.1 draft)
content:
Purpose
This runbook describes the end-to-end process for performing an attested key rotation for customer-managed KMS backed by HSMs inside air-gapped VPCs or on-prem clusters. It focuses on Terraform module interoperability, preflight checks, orchestration steps, audit log capture, and a safe rollback path.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to Redwood Private deployments where customer controls the HSM (Cloud HSM or on-prem HSM appliance) and the Redwood control-plane integrates via a constrained bridge.
- Target scenario: rotate the master wrapping key (KEK) and re-encrypt envelope-wrapped secrets stored in the secrets backplane.
- Assumes existing Terraform modules for kms-hsm-connector and sealed-secrets-operator are in use.
- Assumes an attestation system (attestd) is deployed to each on-prem node to produce hardware-backed attestations.

Non-goals
- This doc does not prescribe hardware vendor commands (vendor-specific HSM CLI). It describes the orchestration and Terraform-level changes.

High-level design overview
- Attestation: each HSM node produces a signed attestation (measurement + public key) that is recorded in the attestation registry.
- New KEK derivation: the HSM generates a new KEK; public material is published to the attestation registry and transparent log.
- Envelope rewrap: secrets stored in the secrets backplane are re-wrapped using the new KEK via a controlled rolling process.
- Audit chain: every step emits structured events to the local audit pipeline (syslog -> audit-forwarder -> central ELK/Tempo) with tamper-evident checkpoints.

Key terminology
- KEK: Key Encrypting Key (wraps DEKs).
- DEK: Data Encryption Key used to encrypt individual secrets.
- Attestation registry: signed store of attestation blobs (immutable append-only).
- Rewrap worker: a short-lived job that re-encrypts secrets with a new KEK.

Preflight checks (must pass before proceeding)
- Terraform plan success for both kms-hsm-connector and sealed-secrets modules in a staging workspace.
- Attestation registry reachable from orchestration host and contains valid attestations for all HSM nodes (check: attest-cli verify --registry <url>).
- Backup: encrypted snapshot of the secrets backplane and current KEK metadata stored off-cluster and checksum-verified.
- Audit forwarding test: generate test-event and verify it appears in central audit index within expected SLA.
- Operator availability: at least 2 on-call SREs and HSM operator available during the maintenance window.

Terraform module notes and change checklist
- New module inputs (suggested):
  - hsm_attestation_blob_url (string) – url to attestation registry blob for new key
  - kek_rotation_id (string) – opaque id used to index the rotation in the state
  - rewrap_batch_size (number) – for the rewrap worker control
  - audit_checkpoint_bucket (string) – where checkpoint manifests are stored
- Outputs to read after apply:
  - kek_public_key_pem
  - rotation_manifest_url
- State handling recommendations:
  - Use a separate Terraform workspace for rotation operations to keep rotation artifacts isolated.
  - If remote state is in an airgapped object store, ensure the connector has a consistent snapshot mechanism (avoid in-place state rewriting during rewrap).
- Upgrade compatibility: the kms-hsm-connector module must be backward compatible to accept both old and new KEK public material for a 7-day overlap window.

Step-by-step rotation procedure (orchestration)
1) Schedule maintenance window and notify customer and internal stakeholders.
2) Create rotation workspace: terraform workspace new rotation-<date>-<id>.
3) Upload attestation artifact for new HSM-generated KEK to registry and record the URL.
4) Terraform change: update kms-hsm-connector module input hsm_attestation_blob_url and set kek_rotation_id. Run terraform plan and apply.
   - Expected effect: connector provisions the new KEK reference and publishes rotation_manifest_url.
5) Verify connector health and that both old and new KEK materials are available to the sealing service.
   - Health checks: /health, /wrap-test (wrap/unwrap a test payload), attestation verify.
6) Start rewrap worker in controlled batches: set rewrap_batch_size to 500 (configurable). Monitor throughput and error rate.
   - Each worker run should post a checkpoint to audit_checkpoint_bucket with: rotation_id, batch_id, start_ts, end_ts, success_count, failure_count, batch_checksum.
7) For any failed items, run a retry worker (idempotent rewrap). Maintain a quarantine list.
8) Once all secrets rewrapped and checkpoints show zero outstanding failures, run finalization: mark rotation manifest as ACTIVE in attestation registry.
9) After a 24–72 hour observation window (business case dependent), remove support for old KEK from sealing service via terraform apply that flips the compatibility flag.
10) Archive rotation artifacts and push a signed rotation summary to the audit index.

Rollback plan (if rewrap causes data loss or unacceptable failures)
- Immediately pause rewrap workers (operator command: rewrapctl pause --rotation <id>).
- Re-enable old KEK in connector if removed prematurely (terraform workspace rotation-<id> apply with compatibility=true).
- Restore secrets backplane from pre-rotation encrypted snapshot into a quarantine namespace and run validation.
- Open an incident (jira:PD-1248) and follow SRE incident runbook.

Audit and observability
- Mandatory event types emitted:
  - rotation.requested (rotation_id, initiator, attestation_blob_url)
  - rotation.kek_generated (hsm_id, public_key_fingerprint, manifest_url)
  - rewrap.batch_completed (batch_id, counts, checksum, worker_id)
  - rotation.finalized (rotation_id, manifest_url, signer)
- Events must be signed with the orchestration key before forwarding to central audit. Use the audit-forwarder agent to attach provider stamps.
- Transparent log: every rotation manifest should be appended to a transparent log (tlog) that supports offline verification.

Attestation verification checklist
- verify attestation signature chain (vendor CA -> HSM attestation cert).
- validate measurements against known-good baseline (firmware hash).
- confirm HSM has not been tampered (physical checks by operator if required).

Operational knobs and timeouts
- rewrap_batch_size: default 500, max 2000 for high-throughput clusters.
- rewrap_worker_timeout: default 15m.
- checkpoint_interval: default 5m.
- compatibility_window_days: default 7 (must be configurable via module input).

Example Terraform pseudo-snippet (conceptual; put in module rotation.tf)

# module "kms_hsm_rotation" {
#   source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-terraform-modules.git//kms-hsm-rotation"
#   hsm_attestation_blob_url = var.hsm_attestation_blob_url
#   kek_rotation_id = var.kek_rotation_id
#   rewrap_batch_size = var.rewrap_batch_size
#   audit_checkpoint_bucket = var.audit_checkpoint_bucket
#}

Operational run commands (examples)
- attest-cli upload --file new-kek-attestation.json --registry https://attest-registry.internal/rotations
- terraform workspace select rotation-2026-02-25-01 && terraform apply -var="hsm_attestation_blob_url=..."
- rewrapctl start --rotation rotation-2026-02-25-01 --batch-size 500
- rewrapctl status --rotation rotation-2026-02-25-01

Testing and canary strategy
- Canary 1: run rewrap worker against non-critical namespace (config: rewrap_batch_size=50). Validate application behavior for 2 hours.
- Canary 2: progressively increase to critical namespaces with monitoring thresholds: error_rate < 0.1%, latency < 200ms for wrap/unwrap calls.

Security considerations
- Minimal privileges: Terraform service principal used for rotation must have least privilege (apply-only to rotation workspace and read against attestation registry).
- Secrets in transit: ensure mTLS between rewrap workers and KMS connector; enforce TLS 1.3 and mutual auth.
- HSM operator authentication must be multi-factor for any key ceremony operation.

Open issues (next steps)
- Add explicit support for threshold HSM (Shamir/K-of-N) in the module (PD-1332).
- Improve attestation registry indexing for faster verification (contrib: attestation-indexer).
- Create a small automated verifier that replays a rotation on a local staging cluster and produces a signed readiness report.

Post-rotation checklist (to be completed and signed off)
- [ ] All rewrap checkpoints show zero outstanding failures.
- [ ] Audit log contains rotation.finalized with signer and manifest URL.
- [ ] Customer notified and acceptance confirmed.
- [ ] Rotation artifacts archived to retention bucket and checksums recorded.
- [ ] Terraform rotation workspace destroyed after 30 days (or retained per customer policy).

Appendix: quick trouble-shooting notes
- wrap-test fails with "invalid-unwrap": check HSM policy binding for the new KEK and ensure public_key PEM matches manifest.
- rewrap worker stuck on item: inspect item metadata in secrets-backplane; try idempotent retry with rewrapctl retry --item <id>.
- attestation verification fails: fetch vendor firmware manifest and compare; if mismatch, escalate to hardware ops.

Owner and on-call
- Owner: Sana Iqbal (eng-private-deployments).
- Primary on-call SRE: Marco Rivera.
- HSM operator: Priya Deshmukh.

Notes and provenance

- Related tickets and PRs listed above. This is a living document — update as modules evolve.
